attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post, stated as his thesis.

semantics.note: Firm 'cannot survive' with an explicit exception clause, so it is a conditional forecast. The nearby disclaimer ('not saying... for sure collapse') fits the conditional framing and does not hedge it. Dropping the 'some possible' aside is harmless.

contract.note: Reading 'a few more years' as up to five years (to 2029-07-29) is an ordinary reading, and it is flagged as the evaluator's. 'Current form' and 'stunning confluence' have no thresholds, so interpretation decides the result. The contract correctly withholds a score while the antecedent is unknown.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own disclosure that its recapitalisation was completed. It bears on 'current form' but does not show survival or failure under the antecedent.
OpenAI's own report of $122B in committed capital. This bears on the financial exception. Committed money is not cash received, and nothing here settles the outcome.

reviews.rationale: The interpreted deadline (July 2029) falls after the evaluation date, and no cessation event has occurred. Whether the antecedent holds (no exceptional mix of technical and financial changes) is unknown; the restructuring and huge fundraising may even meet the exception. Not scorable yet.

attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence in his own post.

semantics.note: This asserts what AI scaling requires, using a historical analogy. It has no outcome or horizon, so it reads as a necessity (causal) claim more than a conditional forecast. The proposition itself is faithful.

contract.note: The contract is right that 'equivalent in ambition' and 'quickly' have no measure, scale target or deadline. Turning them into numbers would add commitments the speaker did not make.

evidence.note: DOE figures on rising data-centre electricity demand and its policy response. These do not test whether an effort on the scale of the New Deal is required.

reviews.rationale: The claim is a qualitative necessity claim built on an analogy of 'ambition'. It sets no amount of AI scaling, no measure of investment and no deadline, so there is no reproducible test. The demand projections are context only.

attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence in his own post.

semantics.note: 'In many ways... R&D facility... dice rigged' is an evaluative analogy, not a checkable observation. The qualifier 'in many ways' is kept.

contract.note: The contract correctly finds no set threshold for when a partnership counts as an R&D facility or for 'rigged' terms. Only the narrow premise, that Microsoft uses OpenAI's technology, is checkable.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own 2023 announcement that its technology is built into Microsoft products. This confirms only the narrow premise, not the analogy or the claim of unfairness.

reviews.rationale: This is a rhetorical, evaluative characterisation with no measurable threshold. The factual premise of integration into Microsoft products is confirmed, but that does not test the whole claim.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post. 'I ultimately believe' introduces the claims as his view; it is not hedging.

semantics.note: A compound, unhedged assertion about present barriers. The normalisation keeps all four parts. It drops the 'theft' framing, which is acceptable.

contract.note: Reading 'no path' as no feasible route is ordinary. The Q2 2024 period was chosen by the evaluator, which is reasonable. 'Too high', 'too much energy' and 'untenable' have no thresholds, so interpretation drives the result.

evidence.note: IEA forecast that demand from data centres, AI and crypto could double by 2026. It neither isolates generative AI nor shows the grid cannot meet the demand.
Peer-reviewed paper projecting data limits for 2026–2032 and listing possible remedies. It shows neither that training was already untenable nor that the problem was solved.

reviews.rationale: None of the evidence settles any of the four parts for the target period. There are no financial records on a path to profitability or on burn, no assessment of generative-AI demand against grid capacity, and the court orders could not be read. The data paper is about possible future limits.
